# elasticstack_kibana_case_field_definition (Resource)

Manages a single field in the Kibana Cases field library. Requires Elastic Stack 9.5.0 or later.

**Technical Preview:** the underlying Kibana API (`/api/cases/field_definitions`) is marked Technical Preview in the Kibana OpenAPI specification, even though the Field Library feature is generally available in the Kibana UI as of 9.5. The API may change in a future release.

The field's shape (type, label, control, metadata, validation) is declared as YAML in `definition`. The field `name` and the YAML `type` are immutable after creation:

- Changing the top-level `name` attribute (together with the matching `name` key in `definition`) replaces the resource.
- Editing only the `name` key inside `definition` so that it no longer matches `name` is rejected by the API with a 400 error.
- Editing the YAML `type` is rejected by the API with a 409 `field_identity_immutable` error.
- Deleting a field that is still referenced by a case template or custom field is rejected with a 409 error.
## Example Usage

```terraform
provider "elasticstack" {
  kibana {}
}

# Minimal field: only owner and definition are required. The field name is
# taken from the `name` key in the YAML.
resource "elasticstack_kibana_case_field_definition" "minimal" {
  owner      = "cases"
  definition = <<-EOT
    name: ticket_reference
    type: keyword
    label: Ticket reference
    control: INPUT_TEXT
  EOT
}

# Field with all optional attributes. `name` must match the `name` key in the
# YAML. `name` and the YAML `type` are immutable: changing `name` replaces the
# resource, while changing only the YAML `type` is rejected by the API with a
# 409 `field_identity_immutable` error.
resource "elasticstack_kibana_case_field_definition" "global" {
  owner       = "securitySolution"
  name        = "customer_tier"
  description = "Support tier of the customer affected by the case."
  is_global   = true
  definition  = <<-EOT
    name: customer_tier
    type: keyword
    label: Customer tier
    control: INPUT_TEXT
  EOT
}

# Field in a non-default Kibana space.
resource "elasticstack_kibana_case_field_definition" "in_space" {
  space_id   = "ops"
  owner      = "observability"
  definition = <<-EOT
    name: runbook_url
    type: keyword
    label: Runbook URL
    control: INPUT_TEXT
  EOT
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `definition` (String) The field definition as a YAML string describing a single field (type, label, control, metadata, validation). Semantically identical YAML is not treated as a change.
- `owner` (String) The solution that owns the field definition: `cases` (Stack), `securitySolution`, or `observability`. Changing this forces a new resource.

### Optional

- `description` (String) Optional human-readable description of the field's purpose.
- `is_global` (Boolean) When true, the field is rendered in every case for this owner regardless of the template used. A global field cannot be set back to false while it is linked to an active custom field.
- `kibana_connection` (Block List) Kibana connection configuration block. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--kibana_connection))
- `name` (String) The field name, unique per owner (case-insensitive). Must match the `name` key in `definition`. When omitted, the server extracts it from `definition`. Immutable: changing this forces a new resource.
- `space_id` (String) An identifier for the space. If space_id is not provided, the default space is used.
- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `display_order` (Number) Position of a global field in the case details view, assigned by the server.
- `field_definition_id` (String) The server-assigned UUID of the field definition.
- `id` (String) The composite ID of the field definition: `<space_id>/<field_definition_id>`.

<a id="nestedblock--kibana_connection"></a>
### Nested Schema for `kibana_connection`

Optional:

- `api_key` (String, Sensitive) API Key to use for authentication to Kibana
- `bearer_token` (String, Sensitive) Bearer Token to use for authentication to Kibana
- `ca_certs` (List of String) A list of paths to CA certificates to validate the certificate presented by the Kibana server.
- `endpoints` (List of String, Sensitive) A comma-separated list of endpoints where the terraform provider will point to, this must include the http(s) schema and port number.
- `insecure` (Boolean) Disable TLS certificate validation
- `password` (String, Sensitive) Password to use for API authentication to Kibana.
- `username` (String) Username to use for API authentication to Kibana.


<a id="nestedatt--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
- `delete` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Setting a timeout for a Delete operation is only applicable if changes are saved into state before the destroy operation occurs.
- `read` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Read operations occur during any refresh or planning operation when refresh is enabled.
- `update` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import elasticstack_kibana_case_field_definition.minimal <space_id>/<field_definition_id>
```
